readme:
# DanceGRPO 共享初噪与组内奖励

## 1. 问题

构造同 prompt 共享的初始噪声、逐奖励通道组内优势，以及逐转移 GRPO 目标。

在小型高斯生成策略中检验多奖励与共享初始条件；不运行视频骨干或视觉奖励模型。

## 2. 核心公式

$$
A_{pg}=\sum_k\frac{R_{pgk}-\mu_{pk}}{\sqrt{\operatorname{mean}_g(R_{pgk}-\mu_{pk})^2}+\varepsilon},\quad L=-\operatorname{mean}_{p,g,t}\min(e^{l_{pgt}}A_{pg},\operatorname{clip}(e^{l_{pgt}},1-c,1+c)A_{pg}).
$$

## 3. 公式到代码

```python
shared_noise(base: Tensor, group_size: int) -> Tensor
```
```python
group_advantages(rewards: Tensor, eps: float=1e-8) -> Tensor
```
```python
dance_loss(log_ratios: Tensor, advantages: Tensor, clip: float) -> Tensor
```

把每个 prompt 的一份初噪复制到组内所有样本。每种奖励分别在组内中心化和缩放，再把通道优势相加。终点优势广播到所有转移，用 clipped 目标更新策略。

## 4. 本题约定

shared_noise accepts base (P,D) and group_size>=2, returns (P,G,D). group_advantages accepts rewards (P,G,K), G>=2; population variance plus eps outside sqrt, sum K. dance_loss log_ratios (P,G,T), advantages (P,G), clip in (0,1), abs(log_ratio)<=40.

Noise and reward-derived advantages are frozen. Only current log ratios differentiate in the policy loss; each prompt is normalized independently.

## 5. 交互图与实验

实验使用你提交的函数。图中各点来自实际运行结果。

Two prompt groups share initial states but draw independent Gaussian actions. Two differently scaled quadratic reward channels train a scalar conditional policy for 70 updates.

## 6. 在网页中运行

在右侧 Python 编辑器中补全实现，点击 **运行测试**。查看失败测试的原因、期望值与实际值，修改代码后再次运行。所有必要测试通过后，题目会标记为已完成并解锁坑点讲解。

## 7. 延伸

比较同 prompt 共享与独立初噪下的组内奖励方差。

[DanceGRPO: Unleashing GRPO on Visual Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.07818) · Section 2.2 Eqs. (9)-(10), Initialization Noise; Section 2.3 combined rewards
notes:
# 题解与常见错误

把每个 prompt 的一份初噪复制到组内所有样本。每种奖励分别在组内中心化和缩放，再把通道优势相加。终点优势广播到所有转移，用 clipped 目标更新策略。

$$
A_{pg}=\sum_k\frac{R_{pgk}-\mu_{pk}}{\sqrt{\operatorname{mean}_g(R_{pgk}-\mu_{pk})^2}+\varepsilon},\quad L=-\operatorname{mean}_{p,g,t}\min(e^{l_{pgt}}A_{pg},\operatorname{clip}(e^{l_{pgt}},1-c,1+c)A_{pg}).
$$

Noise and reward-derived advantages are frozen. Only current log ratios differentiate in the policy loss; each prompt is normalized independently.

不要跨 prompt 标准化，也不要先把不同单位的奖励相加再标准化。常数奖励通道贡献为零。共享初噪不表示后续 SDE 噪声也共享。

测试依据：手算双通道优势、prompt 隔离、常数通道、共享噪声副本、正负截断和冻结梯度。

## 实验标定

固定种子 42，CPU float64，直接梯度下降；无需数据下载。以下是参考解实际测量，不是预设轨迹。 PyTorch 2.14.1. lr=.03 (70 updates).

```json
{"final_error": 0.00024607032777813887, "initial_error": 1.0, "prompt_groups": 2}
```

验收阈值见 `tests/test_core.py::test_real_toy_experiment`；基线为训练前参数的实际输出。

en.title: DanceGRPO Shared Initial Noise and Group Rewards
en.readme:
# DanceGRPO Shared Initial Noise and Group Rewards

## 1. Problem

Construct shared initial noise per prompt, per-reward group advantages and a transition-level GRPO objective.

Test multiple rewards and shared initial conditions in a small Gaussian policy; no video backbone or visual reward model.

## 2. Core equations

$$
A_{pg}=\sum_k\frac{R_{pgk}-\mu_{pk}}{\sqrt{\operatorname{mean}_g(R_{pgk}-\mu_{pk})^2}+\varepsilon},\quad L=-\operatorname{mean}_{p,g,t}\min(e^{l_{pgt}}A_{pg},\operatorname{clip}(e^{l_{pgt}},1-c,1+c)A_{pg}).
$$

## 3. From equations to code

```python
shared_noise(base: Tensor, group_size: int) -> Tensor
```
```python
group_advantages(rewards: Tensor, eps: float=1e-8) -> Tensor
```
```python
dance_loss(log_ratios: Tensor, advantages: Tensor, clip: float) -> Tensor
```

Replicate one initial noise vector across each prompt group. Center and scale each reward channel within its own group, then sum channel advantages. Broadcast terminal advantages to transitions and apply the clipped objective.

## 4. Contract

shared_noise accepts base (P,D) and group_size>=2, returns (P,G,D). group_advantages accepts rewards (P,G,K), G>=2; population variance plus eps outside sqrt, sum K. dance_loss log_ratios (P,G,T), advantages (P,G), clip in (0,1), abs(log_ratio)<=40.

Noise and reward-derived advantages are frozen. Only current log ratios differentiate in the policy loss; each prompt is normalized independently.

## 5. Visualization and experiment

The experiment calls your submitted functions; plotted points are measured results.

Two prompt groups share initial states but draw independent Gaussian actions. Two differently scaled quadratic reward channels train a scalar conditional policy for 70 updates.

## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Extensions

Compare within-group reward variance under shared and independent initial noise.

[DanceGRPO: Unleashing GRPO on Visual Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.07818) · Section 2.2 Eqs. (9)-(10), Initialization Noise; Section 2.3 combined rewards
en.notes:
# Solution reasoning and pitfalls

Replicate one initial noise vector across each prompt group. Center and scale each reward channel within its own group, then sum channel advantages. Broadcast terminal advantages to transitions and apply the clipped objective.

$$
A_{pg}=\sum_k\frac{R_{pgk}-\mu_{pk}}{\sqrt{\operatorname{mean}_g(R_{pgk}-\mu_{pk})^2}+\varepsilon},\quad L=-\operatorname{mean}_{p,g,t}\min(e^{l_{pgt}}A_{pg},\operatorname{clip}(e^{l_{pgt}},1-c,1+c)A_{pg}).
$$

Noise and reward-derived advantages are frozen. Only current log ratios differentiate in the policy loss; each prompt is normalized independently.

Do not normalize across prompts or combine differently scaled rewards before normalization. A constant reward channel contributes zero. Shared initial noise does not require sharing later SDE draws.

Test basis: Hand-computed two-channel advantages, prompt isolation, constant channels, shared-noise copies, signed clipping and frozen gradients.

## Experiment calibration

Seed 42, CPU float64, direct gradient descent, no downloaded data. Values below were measured from the reference, not a preset trajectory. PyTorch 2.14.1. lr=.03 (70 updates).

```json
{"final_error": 0.00024607032777813887, "initial_error": 1.0, "prompt_groups": 2}
```

Acceptance thresholds are in `tests/test_core.py::test_real_toy_experiment`; the baseline is the measured output before training.
